rounds.text: Deepa Jewellers Ltd is dramatically under-appreciated, trading at a modest P/E of 21.9x [E1] while delivering extraordinary capital efficiency that completely dwarfs sector benchmarks. Specifically, the company generates an ROA of 29.5%, an ROE of 44.02%, and an ROCE of 41.29%, crushing the respective sector benchmarks of 4.96%, 8.65%, and 10.27% [E7, E8, E9]. This phenomenal fundamental performance is further reinforced by filed statements showing an even higher ROCE of 51.6% and ROE of 56.4% [E11, E12], alongside a stellar 5-year median ROE of 43% [E17]. Growth is accelerating rapidly, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 28% and profit growth of 68%, which violently accelerate in the trailing twelve months to 38% sales growth and a staggering 158% profit growth [E13, E14, E15, E16]. This compounding engine is backed by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 444 per share—leaving a massive 43.5% margin of safety against the market price of Rs 251—while a reverse DCF shows the current price only prices in a modest 10.2% earnings growth against a base case of 18.0% [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, high insider alignment is secured by a robust 72.98% promoter holding as of September 2026 [E29]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -15 Cr in Mar 2026 with a cash conversion of -0.14x [E23, E24], and debtor days have increased from 37.9 to 47.8 days [E40].

Conceded: [E15]. Despite reported profit growth, Deepa Jewellers Ltd exhibits severe cash flow distress, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -15 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -19 Cr in Mar 2026 [E24, E25]. This translates to a deeply concerning cash conversion ratio of -0.14x against reported profit [E23]. Compounding this disconnect between earnings and actual cash generation, borrowings have escalated to Rs 117 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 81 Cr a year prior, while debtor days have stretched upward from 37.9 to 47.8 days [E27, E40]. Furthermore, filed statements explicitly flag a critical accounting warning that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E39]. Finally, the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 4.68x, which sits more than double the sector benchmark of 2.02x, alongside a total lack of shareholder return through dividends at 0.00% [E3, E6].

Conceded: [E23, E24, E25, E39, E40]. While operating cash flow and debtor metrics require monitoring, they are dwarfed by extraordinary top-line expansion, with 3-year compounded sales growth at 28% and TTM sales growth surging to 38% [E13, E14]. Profitability metrics completely invalidate concerns of fundamental weakness, delivering a stellar 3-year median ROE of 45% and an elite ROCE of 51.6% that pulverize sector benchmarks of 10.27% and 8.65% [E8, E9, E12, E18]. The higher price-to-book ratio of 4.68x versus the sector's 2.02x is entirely justified by this superior capital efficiency and a blistering 158% TTM profit growth rate, which crushes the sector median profit growth of 20.2% [E6, E16, E48]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model explicitly projects intrinsic value at Rs 444 per share, offering a substantial 43.5% margin of safety from current trading levels [E33, E34]. Finally, the reverse DCF confirms that the market price merely prices in a modest 10.2% growth expectation, ignoring the company's proven ability to compound earnings at 68% over three years [E15, E35].

Conceded: [E13, E14, E15, E16, E18, E33, E34, E35]. While the bull highlights impressive growth and valuation models, these figures are fundamentally undermined by the company's inability to convert reported profits into actual cash, as evidenced by a negative cash conversion ratio of -0.14x [E23]. The reliance on accounting profit is further cast into doubt by the explicit warning that the company may be capitalizing interest costs [E39], which artificially inflates earnings at the expense of long-term financial health. This disconnect between paper profits and liquidity is compounded by a deterioration in working capital efficiency, with debtor days ballooning from 37.9 to 47.8 days [E40]. Furthermore, the company’s aggressive expansion is being funded by a significant increase in debt, which rose from Rs 81 Cr to Rs 117 Cr in just one year [E27]. Relying on high ROE and ROCE metrics [E8, E9, E12] is precarious when the underlying operating cash flow is negative [E24] and free cash flow is a deficit of Rs 19 Cr [E25].
